data.trails.livadi-trail.localSecret: Short and sweet. Black pine forest. Ideal for first-timers or families.
data.trails.livadi-trail.name: Livadi Trail
data.trails.livadi-trail.winterNotes: Often clear when higher trails have snow. Good for families.
data.trails.loumata-ton-aeton.descriptio: Linear trail in the Troodos Forest, around 1,100 metres elevation. Green pine forest, narrow valleys. 'Loumata ton Aeton' means Valley of the Eagles. Short but steep in places; ground can be rough. Allow an hour and a half. Good for a leg-stretcher or combined with Kampos tou Livadiou. Winter brings crisp air. Arrange transport for the linear route.
data.trails.loumata-ton-aeton.localSecre: Valley of the Eagles. Short but characterful. Combine with Kampos tou Livadiou for a full morning.
data.trails.loumata-ton-aeton.name: Loumata ton Aeton
data.trails.loumata-ton-aeton.winterNote: Can be muddy. Steep sections. Linear—arrange transport.
data.trails.machairas-forest.description: Forest trail around Machairas Monastery. Pine and golden oak; mountain views. The monastery sits at 870m. The trail winds through the surrounding forest. Moderate grade; allow three hours. Winter: crisp air, fewer visitors. Combine with the monastery, Agros, or a Nicosia hinterland day. About an hour from Nicosia. The monastery café does a good post-hike coffee.
data.trails.machairas-forest.localSecret: The monastery is the centrepiece. Forest trail, mountain air. Agros for loukoumi and rose products after.
data.trails.machairas-forest.name: Machairas Forest Trail
data.trails.machairas-forest.winterNotes: Good winter hike. Monastery at 870m; wrap up. Often clear when Troodos has snow.
data.trails.madari-ridge.description: Eight kilometres along the Madari Ridge. When the day is clear, 360° views over Pitsilia and Troodos. The fire watchtower marks the high point. Pine forest, open ridges, a stretch of the E4 long-distance trail. In winter the ridge can be windy. Snow sometimes settles in January and February. Check the forecast. On clear days the coast stretches out. A misty one still has its atmosphere; the forest closes in, the tower emerges from the cloud. Allow four or five hours. Bring layers. The ridge exposes you.
data.trails.madari-ridge.localSecret: The fire watchtower at km 2.5. Climb it if you can. The 360° views are worth the extra steps. Kyperounta Winery is nearby; highest vineyard in Cyprus. Combine if you have time.
data.trails.madari-ridge.name: Madari Ridge Walk
data.trails.madari-ridge.trailhead: Madari car park (Kyperounta to Spilia road)
data.trails.madari-ridge.winterNotes: Can be windy. Snow on ridge in Jan to Feb. On clear days the coast stretches out.
data.trails.madari-ridge.winterSafety: Ridge is exposed; wind chill significant. Snow possible Jan to Feb. 360° views on clear days. Emergency: 112.
data.trails.mesa-potamos.description: Unofficial loop near Moniatis. Waterfall cascading 7 m, cold river, Timiou Prodromou Monastery (15th century). Mostly dirt roads; family-friendly. Pine and walnut forest. Winter: mild; good for a capital escape. About 30 km from Limassol. Combine with Saittas or Krasochoria wineries.
data.trails.mesa-potamos.localSecret: From Limassol: Saittas road, Kato Amiantos. Look for waterfall signs. The monastery is the surprise.
data.trails.mesa-potamos.name: Mesa Potamos Waterfall
data.trails.mesa-potamos.winterNotes: Mild. Good winter option. Spring for peak flow.
data.trails.millomeris-falls.description: Millomeris is the gentler cousin of Caledonia Falls. Two and a half kilometres, easy grade, wooden walkways and steps. The waterfall drops fifteen metres into a pool. In winter the flow is strong after rain. Families manage it. You can be there and back in under two hours. The trailhead is signed from Pano Platres. The path follows the stream. Moss on the rocks. The sound of water. It's a half-day option when you don't want a full mountain workout, or when the weather suggests something shorter. Combine with a coffee in Platres. The village knows how to warm you up.
data.trails.millomeris-falls.localSecret: Do Millomeris in the morning, then Platres for lunch. The trout tavernas or a café by the river. It's a gentle half-day. Ideal when you don't want a full mountain push.
data.trails.millomeris-falls.name: Millomeris Falls
data.trails.millomeris-falls.winterNotes: Muddy after rain. Waterfall impressive in winter/spring.
data.trails.millomeris-falls.winterSafet: Family-friendly. Wooden walkways can be slippery when wet. Waterfall flow peaks after rain. Shorter and easier than Caledonia.
data.trails.mnimata-piskopon.description: Linear trail commemorating three Cypriot bishops murdered in the Ottoman period. Starts at Kampos tou Livadiou picnic site; first kilometre is wheelchair-accessible. Dense black pine, cliff-edge views over Chromius River, Solea Valley, Morfou Bay. Connects to Kampos tou Livadiou trail. Terminates at forest road to Platania, Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis, or Kakopetria. NATURA 2000. Allow three hours. Fit hikers only; arrange transport for the linear route.
data.trails.mnimata-piskopon.localSecret: The first km is accessible. The views from the cliff edges are the reward. Kakopetria for lunch at the end.
data.trails.mnimata-piskopon.name: Mnimata Piskopon
data.trails.mnimata-piskopon.trailhead: Kampos tou Livadiou picnic site (Troodos–Karvounas road)
data.trails.mnimata-piskopon.winterNotes: Check conditions; can be snowy. Linear—arrange transport at both ends.
data.trails.moutti-anemwn.description: Peak of Winds. A hidden gem in the remote Paphos forest. Linear trail from Pano Panagia toward Stavros tis Psokas; shares a trailhead with Gefyria. Ridgeline walking, 360° views, fewer visitors than Troodos. The Paphos forest feels wilder—more untamed. Check GPS near the end; one junction can lead astray.
data.trails.moutti-anemwn.localSecret: Combine with Gefyria for a longer day. The Paphos forest has a different character to Troodos.
data.trails.moutti-anemwn.name: Moutti twn Anemwn
data.trails.moutti-anemwn.trailhead: Pano Panagia, road toward Stavros tis Psokas
data.trails.moutti-anemwn.winterNotes: Quiet in winter. Windy on the peak—hence the name.
data.trails.moutti-athasias.description: A quiet path, chosen among locals. Near Vavatsinia, the trail follows a scenic forest road before narrowing into woodland. At the end: a mysterious cave—Venetian-era mine for gold and copper. Do not enter; it goes deep and is unmaintained. The cave marks the turnaround. Easy, beginner-friendly. Limited parking.
data.trails.moutti-athasias.localSecret: Chosen by locals, not tourists. Combine with Karvounarka for a longer loop.
data.trails.moutti-athasias.name: Moutti tis Athasias (Cave)
data.trails.moutti-athasias.winterNotes: Ideal winter walk. Cool forest. Cave is the reward.
data.trails.mylikouri.description: Forest trail near Kakopetria. Pine, streams, mountain air. Moderate grade. Allow two hours. Winter: crisp; often clear. Combine with Kakopetria trout tavernas, Kampos tou Livadiou, or Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis. A Solea Valley classic.
data.trails.mylikouri.localSecret: Solea Valley classic. Forest, streams. Kakopetria trout rewards.
data.trails.mylikouri.name: Mylikouri Nature Trail
data.trails.mylikouri.winterNotes: Crisp in winter. Often clear. Kakopetria for trout after.
data.trails.olympus-summit.description: Cyprus's highest peak. 1,952 metres. Winter: snow and ice common Jan–Mar. Microspikes needed. Steep ascent through black pine; 360-degree view on clear days. Start early; cloud builds by midday. Check conditions. Ski resort café at trailhead.
data.trails.olympus-summit.localSecret: On clear winter days you can see both coasts. Start early; cloud often builds by midday. Ski resort café for post-hike warmth.
data.trails.olympus-summit.name: Olympus Summit Trail
data.trails.olympus-summit.trailhead: Troodos Ski Resort / Charalambos the Goat Shepherd
data.trails.olympus-summit.waypoints.0.n: Park at Troodos Ski; check if road is open
data.trails.olympus-summit.winterNotes: Snow/ice common Jan to Mar. Microspikes recommended. Check resort status; ski area may restrict access.
data.trails.olympus-summit.winterSafety: Snow and ice common Jan to Mar. Microspikes or crampons often required. Check ski resort status; access may be restricted. Do not attempt in whiteout or high wind. Emergency: 112.
data.trails.panagia-tis-amasgou.descript: Easy loop in the Limassol hills. The trail passes the church of Panagia tis Amasgou and winds through olive groves and scrub. Gentle grade; family-friendly. Winter sun, mild temps. Combine with Monagri, Omodos, or a Krasochoria winery visit. A relaxed morning or afternoon option.
data.trails.panagia-tis-amasgou.localSec: Gentle, quiet. Olive groves and winter light. Krasochoria wineries nearby.
data.trails.panagia-tis-amasgou.name: Panagia tis Amasgou Trail
data.trails.panagia-tis-amasgou.winterNo: Easy winter walk. Mild. Good for families.
data.trails.panthea.description: Remote ridge on the Kykkos–Tsakistra road. A refuge at the start—jewelry hidden in plain sight. First section: ridgeline with continuous views; then mountain peaks, gravel road toward Kampos or Tsakistra. Park at both ends for one-way, or out-and-back. Best in winter; cloudy days add atmosphere. Shares area with Gnafkio.
data.trails.panthea.localSecret: The refuge at the start is magical. Park cars at both ends for a one-way hike.
data.trails.panthea.name: Panthea Natural Trail
data.trails.panthea.winterNotes: Best in winter. Cloudy weather adds drama.
data.trails.pentadaktylos.description: Foothills of the Five Fingers mountain. Views of the coast and the range. Easy grade. Note: access from south Cyprus; check current routes. Combine with Bellapais, St Hilarion, or coastal Kyrenia. Winter: mild on the coast; the mountains frame the view.
data.trails.pentadaktylos.localSecret: Five Fingers. Coast and range. Bellapais abbey in view.
data.trails.pentadaktylos.name: Pentadaktylos Foothills
data.trails.pentadaktylos.winterNotes: Mild. Coast views. Check access. Bellapais and St Hilarion nearby.
data.trails.persephone-extended.descript: Extended variant of the Persephone trail. More distance, more forest. Troodos heartland. Moderate grade. Allow nearly three hours. Winter: check conditions; can be cool. Platres for lunch. Connects to the wider Troodos network.
data.trails.persephone-extended.localSec: More Persephone. Forest, mountain. Platres trout after.
data.trails.persephone-extended.name: Persephone Extended Loop
data.trails.persephone-extended.winterNo: Cool at elevation. Often clear. Platres nearby.
data.trails.persephone.description: The Persephone Trail runs through the Paphos Forest. Five kilometres, moderate grade. Named after the goddess of spring, and the name pays off in late winter when the clearings fill with cyclamen and anemones. February and March are the sweet spot. The trail has more variety than Artemis; forest, open sections, views of the western Troodos range. It's quieter too. Fewer people. More room to notice the small things. Can be snowy at elevation, so check conditions. If the weather holds, it's one of the loveliest walks in the mountains. Start from Troodos Square. Kakopetria and Caledonia Falls are within reach for a full day.
data.trails.persephone.localSecret: Late Feb to early Mar: look for cyclamen and anemones in the clearings. Less crowded than Artemis.
data.trails.persephone.name: Persephone Trail
data.trails.persephone.waypoints.0.name: Troodos Square
data.trails.persephone.waypoints.1.name: Forest clearings
data.trails.persephone.waypoints.2.name: Western loop
data.trails.persephone.winterNotes: Feb to Mar wildflowers. Can be snowy at elevation; check summit conditions.
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.description: A coastal walk that strings together one of Cyprus's most famous landmarks; Petra tou Romiou, Aphrodite's Rock; with quiet stretches of shoreline. You start near the viewpoint car park and follow paths and tracks that keep the sea in sight. In winter the light is softer, the crowds gone. Waves break on the rocks, the air smells of salt and wild thyme. The route is mostly easy underfoot, with one or two short climbs to low bluffs for better views along the coast toward Pissouri. It's a half-day option when the mountains feel too cold. Pair it with a village lunch inland or a visit to Kourion or the Pafos mosaics to round out the day.
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.localSecret: Walk east toward the quieter coves once you've had your fill of Aphrodite's Rock. The low bluffs give better views for photos, especially late afternoon when the light drops behind you.
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.name: Petra tou Romiou Coastal Walk
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.trailhead: Petra tou Romiou viewpoint car park, old Paphos to Limassol road
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.waypoints.1: Famous landmark; rocky shore, strong currents
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.waypoints.2: Low cliffs with long views toward Pissouri
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.waypoints.3: Turnaround point; return the same way
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.winterNotes: Ideal winter walk; mild temperatures and fewer people. Waves can be stronger after storms; stay well back from the waterline on rough days.
data.trails.petra-tou-romiou.winterSafet: Do not swim here; currents are strong even on calm days. Stay back from the waterline in winter storms; rogue waves can reach higher than expected. Coastal wind can be brisk; bring a layer.
data.trails.pissouromoutti.description: Short loop from Smigies picnic site. Pissouromoutti peak at 420 metres. Pine forest, scenic views over the Akamas peninsula and Chrysochou Bay. Nearly a third of the trail is shaded; kid-friendly. May cross a riverbed after rain. Winter temps are ideal. Combine with Smigies long route or Adonis for a full Akamas day. Polis and Vasilikon winery on the loop back.
data.trails.pissouromoutti.localSecret: The summit views open out at 420m. Combine with Smigies long route for a full morning. Polis for lunch.
data.trails.pissouromoutti.name: Pissouromoutti Trail
data.trails.pissouromoutti.winterNotes: Ideal winter hike. Cool, shaded sections. Riverbed may be wet after rain.
data.trails.politiko-machairas.descripti: A hidden sanctuary. Gorge, stream, Grigoris Afxentiou hideout, Machairas Monastery. The path follows the Pediaios River through a vast ravine; a bridge halfway crosses the mountainside. Magical after rain—the stream runs strong, the forest turns vivid green. Linear; both ends accessible by car. Experienced hikers can extend to Lazanias or Fikardou.
data.trails.politiko-machairas.localSecr: Go after rain. The bridge crossing is the highlight. Machairas café for post-hike warmth.
data.trails.politiko-machairas.name: Politiko to Machairas
data.trails.politiko-machairas.winterNot: Winter is magic—stream flows, greenery. First half exposed; second half shaded.
data.trails.potamia-dam.description: Circular route around Potamia Dam. Water views, birdlife, gentle grade. Easy; suitable for all. About 40 minutes from Nicosia. Winter: mild; good for a capital escape. Combine with Agros, Machairas, or Nicosia old town.
data.trails.potamia-dam.localSecret: Dam, birds, water. Easy capital escape. Agros for loukoumi after.
data.trails.potamia-dam.name: Potamia Dam Trail
data.trails.potamia-dam.winterNotes: Mild. Good capital escape. Dam and water views.
data.trails.sea-caves-anargyroi.descript: Linear coastal trail from Agioi Anargyroi. Sea caves, Kamara tou Koraka natural bridge, cliffside formations. E4 path. Winter brings fewer crowds than summer. Turquoise water, limestone. Easy underfoot.
data.trails.sea-caves-anargyroi.localSec: Start at Agioi Anargyroi, walk toward Blue Lagoon. The caves are the reward.
data.trails.sea-caves-anargyroi.name: Sea Caves – Agioi Anargyroi
data.trails.sea-caves-anargyroi.winterNo: Winter = fewer crowds. Mild. Ideal coastal walk.
data.trails.selladi-stavros.description: Forest trail in the Troodos heartland. Pine, ridges, mountain views. Moderate grade; allow two and a half hours. Winter can bring snow at elevation; check conditions. Connects to the wider Troodos trail network. Platres or Kakopetria for lunch. A solid half-day in the mountains.
data.trails.selladi-stavros.localSecret: Quieter than Artemis. Ridge and forest. Platres for trout after.
data.trails.selladi-stavros.name: Selladi tis Stavros
data.trails.selladi-stavros.winterNotes: Check conditions; snow possible. Often clear in December or March.
data.trails.selladi-trypilos.description: Remote Cedar Valley. Linear trail through endemic cedar and pine; Trypilos fire lookout at 1,400 m offers 360° views. Parking for 6–7 cars. Part of E4. Winter can bring snow and fog. The cedars are the draw—horizontal layers, distinctive. Access via Panagia or Kykkos.
data.trails.selladi-trypilos.localSecret: Parking fills fast. Go early. The cedars are unlike anywhere else on the island.
data.trails.selladi-trypilos.name: Selladi tou Staxtou – Trypilos
data.trails.selladi-trypilos.winterNotes: Snow and fog possible. Check conditions. Limited parking.
data.trails.smigies.description: A circular trail at Smigies picnic site, five kilometres from Neo Chorio in the centre of the Akamas peninsula. Dense forest, old disused magnesium mines with abandoned kilns, and a connection with the Adonis Trail at Kefalovrysia. Views of Lara Bay, Chrysochou Bay, Latsi, Polis, and the Paphos Forest. Endemic flora and fauna—Cyprus germander, Cyprus viper. Winter temps are ideal; cooler than summer, fewer crowds. The long route rewards with forest solitude. Allow two to three hours. Combine with Vasilikon or Sterna winery and Polis for lunch.
data.trails.smigies.localSecret: The long route passes the abandoned kilns; a slice of Akamas history. Connect with Adonis at Kefalovrysia if you want a longer day.
data.trails.smigies.name: Smigies Nature Trail
data.trails.smigies.trailhead: Smigies picnic site, near Neo Chorio
data.trails.smigies.winterNotes: Ideal winter hike. Cool temps, forest shade. Some muddy patches after rain.
data.trails.stavros-tis-psokas.descripti: Forest station trail in the heart of Akamas. Stavros tis Psokas is a forestry outpost; the trail winds through pine and scrub with wildlife spotting opportunities—mouflon, if you're lucky. Remote, quieter than the Baths of Aphrodite area. Winter brings crisp air and fewer visitors. Allow two to three hours. The drive in is part of the adventure; rough in places. Combine with Polis or Latsi for a coastal lunch on the way back.
data.trails.stavros-tis-psokas.localSecr: Mouflon sometimes spotted early morning. The forestry road in can be adventurous; 4x4 helps in wet weather.
data.trails.stavros-tis-psokas.name: Stavros tis Psokas
data.trails.stavros-tis-psokas.winterNot: Cool and quiet in winter. Road can be rough; check conditions. Fewer people than coastal trails.
data.trails.stavrovouni.description: Circular trail around the cliffside Stavrovouni Monastery. Punishing ascents, technical descents, rocky terrain. Steep and demanding. Rewards: 360° views of Larnaca, Salt Lake, Mediterranean, Troodos, Famagusta. Best in winter; fully exposed, no shade. Combine with Agia Varvara for ~10 km. Hiking poles recommended.
data.trails.stavrovouni.localSecret: Go clockwise—signs are visible that way. Combine with Agia Varvara–Stavrovouni for a big day.
data.trails.stavrovouni.name: Stavrovouni Nature Trail
data.trails.stavrovouni.winterNotes: Best in winter. Exposed—no shade. Avoid when raining.
data.trails.trees-of-woe.description: Historic trail; the name recalls a darker past. Today: forest, mountain air, Troodos character. Moderate grade. Allow nearly three hours. Winter: crisp; can be cool. Platres or Kakopetria for lunch. Part of the Troodos narrative.
data.trails.trees-of-woe.localSecret: The name tells a story. Forest, mountain. Troodos character.
data.trails.trees-of-woe.name: Trees of Woe Trail
data.trails.trees-of-woe.winterNotes: Crisp. Cool at elevation. Platres or Kakopetria after.
data.trails.vavatsinia-honeybee.descript: The Humming of the Bees. A 2.5 km nature path in Agioi Vavatsinias village, Larnaca uplands. Bee-themed: bee-friendly plants, decorative beehives, bee hotels. Hexagonal wooden pavilions and benches. Educational and restorative. Suitable for all fitness levels. Winter is quiet; the village sits at 700m. Combine with Lefkara, Stavrovouni, or Choirokoitia for a full Larnaca hinterland day.
data.trails.vavatsinia-honeybee.localSec: One of the nine Rural Larnaka Honey Villages. Apitherapy and bee communication info along the path.
data.trails.vavatsinia-honeybee.name: Vavatsinia Honeybee Trail
data.trails.vavatsinia-honeybee.winterNo: Easy winter walk. Village at 700m; wrap up. Quiet and peaceful.
data.trails.vouni-panagias.description: Forest trail in the Laona hills. Vouni Panagias village sits above the Paphos wine route. The trail winds through scrub and pine with valley views. Combine with Vouni Panayia winery—one of Cyprus's most awarded—for a full Laona day. Winter brings crisp air and fewer visitors. Allow two to three hours. Panayia village for lunch.
data.trails.vouni-panagias.localSecret: Combine with Vouni Panayia winery. The Laona route rewards those who hike and taste.
data.trails.vouni-panagias.name: Vouni Panagias Nature Trail
data.trails.vouni-panagias.winterNotes: Ideal winter hike. Cool, quiet. Perfect with Vouni Panayia winery.
data.trails.vretsia-roudias.description: Abandoned village, Venetian bridge, ruined watermill. Vretsia was evacuated after 1974; the trail feels like walking through an open museum. The Roudias bridge over the Xeros River is the jewel—stone arches, cool shade, lush vegetation. Circular route: start from Vretsia, follow the gravel road to the bridge, return via the trail. Remote Paphos forest. Winter brings crisp air and solitude.
data.trails.vretsia-roudias.localSecret: Do not attempt from Agios Ioannis—use Vretsia. The watermill ruins halfway add to the sense of time.
data.trails.vretsia-roudias.name: Vretsia – Roudias Venetian Bridge
data.trails.vretsia-roudias.winterNotes: Quiet in winter. Cool forest. Road to Vretsia can feel like the wrong way—keep going.
data.trails.xyliatos-dam.description: Circular route through the Adelfoi forest. Views of Xyliatos Dam and surrounding mountains. Easy grade; suitable for all. About 50 minutes from Nicosia. Winter brings crisp air and fewer visitors. The ascending start is the hardest section; the rest rewards with dam and forest views. Picnic area at the trailhead. Combine with Kakopetria or Agros for a Nicosia hinterland day.
data.trails.xyliatos-dam.localSecret: A Sunday favourite. The dam views open up as you climb. Quiet in winter.
data.trails.xyliatos-dam.name: Xyliatos Dam Natural Trail
data.trails.xyliatos-dam.winterNotes: Easy winter walk. Mild. Good for families. Dam and forest.
data.weather.April.coastDesc: Warm. Some swim. Easter dates vary; villages come alive.
data.weather.April.troodosDesc: Mountain green. All trails open. Spring clarity.
data.weather.December.coastDesc: Mild days, cool nights. Layers. Christmas markets and mulled wine.
data.weather.December.troodosDesc: Snow possible from mid‑month. Ski resort opens. Check trail conditions.
data.weather.February.coastDesc: Similar to January. Almond blossoms from late Feb. Longer days.
data.weather.February.troodosDesc: Ski season continues. Late Feb trails start to clear. Crocus and cyclamen.
data.weather.January.coastDesc: Coolest month. Still sunny. Ruins and villages; pack a warm layer.
data.weather.January.troodosDesc: Peak ski season. Trails may be icy. Book tastings; wineries warm inside.
data.weather.March.coastDesc: Spring light. Wildflowers inland. Sea still cold; beach walks fine.
data.weather.March.troodosDesc: Best hiking month. Snow melts, trails open. Persephone trail blooms.
data.weather.November.coastDesc: Still mild. Light jacket for evenings. Beaches empty, ruins at their best.
data.weather.November.troodosDesc: Cool mornings. Trails clear. Ski season not yet; best for hiking.
data.wineries.adege.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; combine with Omodos or Louvaras.
data.wineries.adege.description: Family-run in Vasa, one of the quieter Krasochoria villages. Their Lefkada is worth the drive. Warm welcome, mountain air. Call ahead; they appreciate the heads-up. Combine with Omodos or Louvaras for a full village day. The kind of place where someone pours and then sits down to talk.
data.wineries.adege.localSecret: Vasa is quieter than Omodos. Mountain air and Lefkada. Reserve—they appreciate it.
data.wineries.adege.name: Adege Winery
data.wineries.adege.winterTip: Family-run in Vasa. Village hospitality; call ahead. Lefkada is worth the drive.
data.wineries.aes-ambelis.description: Founded early 1990s by George Tripatsas. Three hectares; Maratheftiko, Shiraz, Chardonnay; natural farming. ~170,000 bottles/year. Two-level architecture, underground cellar, tasting hall overlooking Pitsilia. Artisanal cheese and charcuterie available.
data.wineries.aes-ambelis.localSecret: Compare Maratheftiko and Xynisteri with other Pitsilia estates.
data.wineries.aes-ambelis.name: Aes Ambelis Winery
data.wineries.aes-ambelis.transport: Kalo Chorio Orinis, 28 km SW of Nicosia.
data.wineries.aes-ambelis.winterTip: 28 km from Nicosia. Terrace views over Pitsilia mountains.
data.wineries.agios-theodoros.descriptio: Agios Theodoros village. Small. Honest. The kind of place where the owner pours. Mavro, Xynisteri, and a sweet wine worth asking about. Call ahead. Off the main Commandaria loop, which means fewer visitors and more room to talk. The wine is straightforward. The welcome is real.
data.wineries.agios-theodoros.localSecre: Small. Authentic. The kind of place where the owner pours. Wine is honest.
data.wineries.agios-theodoros.name: Agios Theodoros Winery
data.wineries.agios-theodoros.winterTip: Off the main loop. Agios Theodoros. Mavro, Xynisteri, sweet wine. Call ahead.
data.wineries.ambeli.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; combine with Platres trails.
data.wineries.ambeli.description: Right in Platres. Forest and vineyard views. Ski in the morning, Ambeli in the afternoon. Or Artemis trail, then taste. Lefkada has character. Winter tastings by the fire. Call ahead in season.
data.wineries.ambeli.localSecret: Lefkada has character. Village knows how to warm you up.
data.wineries.ambeli.name: Ambeli Winery
data.wineries.ambeli.winterTip: Ski or Artemis in the morning, Ambeli in the afternoon. Forest views.
data.wineries.anama.description: Larnaca wine route. Commandaria focus; sweet and semi-sweet. The village setting is peaceful. Book ahead. Combine with Stavrovouni, Choirokoitia, or Zygi for fish. Winter: ideal for Commandaria tastings. The Larnaca hills have their own microclimate.
data.wineries.anama.localSecret: Sweet and semi-sweet. Commandaria in the Larnaca hills. Book and taste.
data.wineries.anama.name: Anama Vintages
data.wineries.anama.winterTip: Larnaca Commandaria. Peaceful village. Combine with Stavrovouni or Zygi.
data.wineries.antoniades.description: Traditional Cypriot wines since the early 20th century. Commandaria—their Nama carries the ancient name, aged in oak for over ten years. Kastelani Red and White from indigenous Mavro and Xynisteri. Special Reserve aged in French oak. Sparkling by the Champagne method. Mandria village, near the Commandaria zone. Tours and tastings; book ahead. Heritage in every bottle.
data.wineries.antoniades.localSecret: Nama: the ancient name of Commandaria. Aged over ten years in oak.
data.wineries.antoniades.name: M. Antoniades Winery
data.wineries.antoniades.winterTip: Their Nama—ancient Commandaria. Ask about the pithari jar heritage.
data.wineries.argyrides.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; combine with Omodos, Koilani.
data.wineries.argyrides.description: Five generations since 1913. Housed in a 200-year-old listed ancestral home in Vasa Koilaniou, meticulously restored. Eight hectares in Laona Krasochoria; Maratheftiko, Xynisteri, Cabernet, Merlot, Chardonnay, Viognier. Modern tech meets tradition. Wine Club for limited editions.
data.wineries.argyrides.localSecret: Wine Club for limited editions. One of the most beautiful wineries in Cyprus.
data.wineries.argyrides.name: Argyrides Winery
data.wineries.argyrides.winterTip: 200-year-old house. Stone holds the sun in winter.
data.wineries.avakas.description: Commercial production since 1988; moved to new premises 2009. Statos at 1,000 m in central Paphos mountains. ~200,000 L/year from 8 ha; Maratheftiko, Ophtalmo. Wines follow Byzantine and Roman traditions. Combine with Avakas Gorge—call from the car park when done; they're used to hikers.
data.wineries.avakas.localSecret: Xynisteri from mountain vines has different character. Ask.
data.wineries.avakas.name: Avakas Winery
data.wineries.avakas.transport: Statos village, 1,000 m. Near Avakas Gorge.
data.wineries.avakas.winterTip: Do Avakas Gorge in the morning, then winery. Call from car park when done—they're used to hikers.
data.wineries.ayia-mavri.description: Established 1983; first winery in Koilani. Run by Yiannoula and Ioannis Ioannidou. ~50,000 bottles/year from Mavro, Xinisteri, Muscat, Lefkada, Shiraz, Cabernet. Famous for Mosxatos sweet wines. Vineyard tour, tastings, local cheese and delicacies.
data.wineries.ayia-mavri.localSecret: Mosxatos sweet wines—ask for a taste.
data.wineries.ayia-mavri.name: Ayia Mavri Winery
data.wineries.ayia-mavri.winterTip: Cosy in winter. Koilani at 900 m; Commandaria and dry wines.
data.wineries.ayii-anargyri.description: Small production in Miliou. Valley views from the terrace. Book ahead. Ideal for a quiet escape on the Laona route. The hills roll away; the Paphos hinterland has its own rhythm.
data.wineries.ayii-anargyri.localSecret: Valley from terrace. Stay. Order another glass.
data.wineries.ayii-anargyri.name: Ayii Anargyri Winery
data.wineries.ayii-anargyri.winterTip: Peaceful Miliou. Valley views. Book ahead.
data.wineries.ayios-savas.description: Coastal Limassol winery. Vineyards near the sea; a different terroir from the mountains. Crisp whites, easy-drinking reds. Tours and tastings; book ahead. Combine with a beach morning at Governor's Beach or a Kourion afternoon. Twenty minutes from Limassol. Winter tastings with sea views.
data.wineries.ayios-savas.localSecret: Sea-influenced terroir. A coastal take on Cypriot wine.
data.wineries.ayios-savas.name: Ayios Savvas Winery
data.wineries.ayios-savas.winterTip: Coastal vines. Different from mountain wine. Governor's Beach and Kourion nearby.
data.wineries.cholettis.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; plan to stay.
data.wineries.cholettis.description: Organic and natural. Statos village, Laona plateau. Book the meze pairing; the cheese and olives make the wine sing. They're passionate about natural fermentation. Ask. The setting is peaceful. Plan to stay. Laona has a different vibe to the Krasochoria: quieter, more remote. Winter tastings feel like a gift.
data.wineries.cholettis.localSecret: Ask about natural fermentation. They're passionate. Statos setting is peaceful.
data.wineries.cholettis.name: Cholettis Winery
data.wineries.cholettis.winterTip: Book the meze pairing. Cheese and olives make the wine sing. Laona plateau has a different vibe.
data.wineries.christoudia.description: Founded 1992 by Yiannis and Alexia Christoudia (originally KRELAN). ~80,000 bottles from Xinisteri, Maratheftiko, Spourtiko, Cabernet, Muscat. Modern facility (2012) with barrel cellars. Fireplace in winter. Brunch with Cypriot cuisine; weddings and events.
data.wineries.christoudia.localSecret: Brunch with Cypriot cuisine. Combine with Lefkara.
data.wineries.christoudia.name: Christoudia Winery
data.wineries.christoudia.winterTip: Fireplace tastings. Kato Drys, Larnaca hills.
data.wineries.chrysoroyiatissa-winery.de: The monastery's own winery, distinct from the Chrysorrogiatissa monastery attraction. Winemaking here dates to 1725; the facility reopened in 1984. Indigenous Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Mavro, plus Shiraz and Cabernet. The spiritual setting—within the monastery grounds—complements the tasting. Book ahead. Panayia village is nearby. Combine with Vouni Panayia winery and the Laona route for a full Paphos hills day.
data.wineries.chrysoroyiatissa-winery.lo: The name means Our Lady of the Golden Pomegranate. The wines carry that heritage.
data.wineries.chrysoroyiatissa-winery.wi: Monastery grounds. Spiritual and vinous. Combine with Vouni Panayia and Panayia village. Laona route gem.
data.wineries.dafermou.description: Larnaca hills winery. Modern facility, indigenous varieties. Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Yiannoudi. Tastings and tours; book ahead. Combine with Lefkara, Stavrovouni, or the Larnaca coast. Winter: mild in the hills. A different side of Cypriot wine.
data.wineries.dafermou.localSecret: Yiannoudi, Xynisteri. A different Larnaca. Book and taste.
data.wineries.dafermou.name: Ktima Dafermou
data.wineries.dafermou.winterTip: Larnaca hills. Modern, indigenous. Mild in winter. Lefkara nearby.
data.wineries.domes-sergiou.backstory: The Sergiou family brings a fresh perspective to Cypriot winemaking. From their base in Skarinou, between Larnaca and Limassol, they work exclusively with indigenous varieties; Xynisteri, Morokanella, Assyrtiko, Maratheftiko; and their Atypon range (the name means 'unexpected') has become a talking point among wine lovers. They sell direct via their online shop and welcome visitors for tastings by appointment.
data.wineries.domes-sergiou.description: The Sergiou family makes wine in Skarinou, between Limassol and Larnaca. Indigenous varieties only: Xynisteri, Morokanella, Assyrtiko, Maratheftiko, and the Atypon blends. They often pour the tastings themselves and tell the story behind each bottle. Book ahead.
data.wineries.domes-sergiou.localSecret: Their Atypon 02 (Assyrtiko & Xynisteri blend) and Rosé Maratheftiko 2024 surprise people who think they know Cypriot wine. Ask about the Atypon range; the name means 'unexpected'.
data.wineries.domes-sergiou.name: Dómes Sergiou
data.wineries.domes-sergiou.transport: Short drive from Larnaca or Limassol (A1). Skarinou exit.
data.wineries.domes-sergiou.winterTip: Skarinou is a short drive from Larnaca or Limassol; ideal for a winter afternoon. Their Atypon 01 red blend and Xynisteri Single Vineyard are standouts. Can't visit? Order online.
data.wineries.etko-olympus.description: Cyprus's oldest winemaker—since 1844. Christodoulos Haggipavlu started the commercial wine business; six generations later, ETKO runs Olympus Winery in Omodos. Commandaria, Cabernet (Ino), Maratheftiko, Xynisteri. Modern plant and equipment, research into new wines. The Omodos facility welcomes visitors. Book ahead. Do the monastery and village first; ETKO completes the Omodos story.
data.wineries.etko-olympus.localSecret: Six generations. Their Commandaria and Ino Cabernet. The story of Cypriot wine in one place.
data.wineries.etko-olympus.name: ETKO / Olympus Winery
data.wineries.etko-olympus.winterTip: Oldest name in Cypriot wine. Omodos village at your feet. Book ahead.
data.wineries.evangelou.description: Where tradition meets the future. Evangelou sits in Pera Pedi, Commandaria heartland. Indigenous varieties, modern techniques. Their Commandaria-style wines and dry offerings attract visitors who want both heritage and quality. The tasting room is warm; book ahead in winter. Pera Pedi is one of the original Commandaria villages. Combine with Omodos, Koilani, or Hadjipavlou for a full village circuit.
data.wineries.evangelou.localSecret: Their Commandaria-style wines. Tradition and modern craft. Pera Pedi rewards those who take their time.
data.wineries.evangelou.name: Evangelou Winery
data.wineries.evangelou.winterTip: Pera Pedi. Commandaria zone. Book ahead. Combine with Omodos and Koilani for a full Krasochoria day.
data.wineries.ezousa.description: Owner Michalis Constantinides. Named after the Ezousa river; four hectares at 400 m. Indigenous varieties only—soils born of fire and time. ~52,000 bottles/year. Tasting room; book ahead.
data.wineries.ezousa.name: Ezousa Winery
data.wineries.ezousa.winterTip: Book the meze pairing. Kannaviou is off the main routes; authentic.
data.wineries.fikardos.description: Founded in 1990 by Theodoros Fikardos, one of the first privately owned wineries in Cyprus. Vineyards in Pano Arodes and Choulou; grapes from Stroumbi, Tsada, Kathikas. Five ranges: Classic, Medium Sweet, Premium, Premium Limited Edition, Experiment. Terrace overlooking the vines.
data.wineries.fikardos.localSecret: Maratheftiko and Giannoudi; ask about Premium Limited Edition.
data.wineries.fikardos.name: Fikardos Winery
data.wineries.fikardos.transport: 22 Michalaki Savvidi, Mesogi. ~10 min from Paphos.
data.wineries.fikardos.winterTip: Terrace catches winter sun. 10 min from Paphos old town, 20 min from harbour.
data.wineries.fikardou-winery.descriptio: Historic village of Fikardou; UNESCO heritage. The wine estate complements the restored stone houses. Small production; book ahead. Combine with the village walk, Machairas, or Agros. Winter: the village is magical; snow possible. A culture and wine day.
data.wineries.fikardou-winery.localSecre: Stone houses, mountain air, small-batch wine. Culture and taste in one.
data.wineries.fikardou-winery.name: Fikardou Wine Estate
data.wineries.fikardou-winery.transport: Fikardou village, UNESCO site. ~50 min from Nicosia.
data.wineries.fikardou-winery.winterTip: UNESCO Fikardou. Village and wine. Snow possible in deep winter. Magical.
data.wineries.hadjicharalambous.descript: HCH Winery is a family-run boutique in the heart of Stroumbi village. Handmade, limited-production wines—around 2,000 bottles a year—from their own vineyards. Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah. Hands-on experiences: grape smashing, juice tasting, bottle filling. The setting in the Paphos hills enhances the tasting. Book ahead; they run a lean operation and appreciate the notice. Winter tastings in the stone-built space feel intimate.
data.wineries.hadjicharalambous.localSec: Their small-batch Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon. The family pours and tells the story. Stroumbi is quieter than Omodos.
data.wineries.hadjicharalambous.name: Hadjicharalambous Boutique Winery
data.wineries.hadjicharalambous.winterTi: Stroumbi village, Paphos hills. Book the hands-on experience if you have time. Part of the Laona route; combine with Fikardos or Tsangarides.
data.wineries.hadjipavlou.description: Third-generation family winery in Pera Pedi, one of the original Commandaria villages at 770 m. Traditional sun-dried grapes, long ageing. Stone cellar, mountain air. Call ahead for tastings.
data.wineries.hadjipavlou.localSecret: Sun-dried grapes, traditional ageing. Pera Pedi is Commandaria heartland.
data.wineries.hadjipavlou.name: Hadjipavlou Winery
data.wineries.hadjipavlou.winterTip: Third-generation family; authentic Commandaria and mountain wines. Stone cellar is cosy in winter.
data.wineries.iona.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; combine with Koilani lunch.
data.wineries.iona.description: Elegant Xynisteri and Maratheftiko in the Krasochoria. Tasting room with Troodos views. Wine-and-cheese pairing worth booking. Koilani village nearby for lunch. Winter mountain light is sharp.
data.wineries.iona.localSecret: Maratheftiko has real character. Ask about single-vineyard releases.
data.wineries.iona.name: Iona Winery
data.wineries.iona.winterTip: Book the wine-and-cheese pairing. Troodos views from the tasting room.
data.wineries.kalamos.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; combine with Paphos or Akamas.
data.wineries.kalamos.description: Family-owned by Nicos Ignatiou and sons. Mataro, Xynisteri, Maratheftiko; Commandaria, liqueurs, Zivania. ~20 min from Paphos. Quality local wines—red, white, dry, semi-dry, sweet. Direct delivery of limited editions.
data.wineries.kalamos.localSecret: Commandaria and Zivania. Limited editions available.
data.wineries.kalamos.name: Kalamos Winery
data.wineries.kalamos.transport: Kira Eleni 6, Amargeti 8642. ~20 min from Paphos.
data.wineries.karseras.description: Commandaria pioneers on the Laona border. Karseras helped revive modern Commandaria production. Traditional sun-dried grapes, barrel ageing. The tasting room is cosy; the story of how they brought Commandaria back to the fore is worth hearing. Near Platres; combine with a morning trail. Call ahead in winter. Their Commandaria stands up to the best.
data.wineries.karseras.localSecret: They helped pioneer the modern Commandaria comeback. Ask about the sun-drying process.
data.wineries.karseras.name: Karseras Winery
data.wineries.karseras.winterTip: Near Platres. Do Artemis or Caledonia in the morning, Karseras in the afternoon. Commandaria revival story.
data.wineries.kolios.backstory: The Kolios family has farmed this land for generations. At 3,000 feet, the light calcareous soil and dry, cool summers produce grapes with unique character. Wild mouflons still wander through the vineyards; Paphos forest meets the vines. The winery is a short drive from Chrysorrogiatissa Monastery—combine the two for a perfect Paphos hills day. Wines age in an underground isothermal cellar; the natural spring provides humidity. Several bottles have won gold at the Cyprus Wine Competition.
data.wineries.kolios.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Feb, 11am for tour and lunch. Quieter than summer; heaters indoors.
data.wineries.kolios.description: Kolios sits on a mountaintop about a kilometre outside Statos Agios Fotios, towards Chrysorrogiatissa Monastery. At 3,000 feet, the family cultivates the largest organic Maratheftiko vineyard in Cyprus—no chemical fertilizers, only natural methods. Four generations have tended these vines. The underground cellar has oak barrels and a natural spring that keeps the humidity ideal for ageing. Guided tours at 12:30pm are followed by traditional meze lunch at 1pm, cooked by the owner's wife from local ingredients. Book one or two days ahead. The views over mountainous Paphos—pine-covered slopes, gorges, mouflons wandering the vineyards—reward the drive up.
data.wineries.kolios.localSecret: Their Persefoni (Xynisteri) and Maratheftiko are award-winners. Wines cost €5–14 at the cellar—far below retail. The Iris white, from the rare Spourtiko grape, is a standout. Ask to see the underground cellar; the natural spring runs through it.
data.wineries.kolios.name: Kolios Winery
data.wineries.kolios.openingHours: Winter (Oct–Feb): Mon–Sat 9am–3pm. Summer (Mar–Sep): Mon–Sat 8:30am–5pm. Sunday: private parties only (50+ guests).
data.wineries.kolios.transport: About 25 min from Paphos. From Statos Agios Fotios village, follow signs 1 km toward Chrysorrogiatissa.
data.wineries.kolios.winterTip: Book lunch 1–2 days ahead. Bring cash—they may not take cards. The meze is authentic village food, not tourist meze. February is quiet; the views and wine are worth the drive.
data.wineries.komos.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; late morning before lunch.
data.wineries.komos.description: In the heart of Omodos. Cellar tastings, Commandaria aged the traditional way. Do the monastery and square first, then Komos. Village cafés do lunch. Ask to compare older and younger vintages. Winter visitors get the courtyard mostly to themselves.
data.wineries.komos.localSecret: Compare older and younger Commandaria vintages—you'll taste the difference.
data.wineries.komos.name: Komos Winery
data.wineries.komos.winterTip: Do monastery and square first, then cellar tasting. Village cafés for lunch.
data.wineries.krasas.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; combine with Koilani loop.
data.wineries.krasas.description: Fourth generation. Koilani. Commandaria heartland. Ask to see the cellar; it's historic, and the story is worth hearing. Krasas has been here for generations. It shows in the wine and the welcome. Book ahead. The cellar tour is the gift.
data.wineries.krasas.localSecret: Ask to see the cellar. Koilani Commandaria heartland. Generations of heritage.
data.wineries.krasas.name: Krasas Winery
data.wineries.krasas.winterTip: Fourth generation in Koilani. Historic cellar. Book ahead.
data.wineries.ktima-vassiliades.backstor: Oenou Yi–Ktima Vassiliades; modern facility, traditional Commandaria craft.
data.wineries.ktima-vassiliades.bestTime: Dec to Mar, late morning before lunch.
data.wineries.ktima-vassiliades.descript: Also known as Oenou Yi; founded 2017 by Christodoulos G. Vassiliades. At 800–1,000 m in Commandaria zone. Traditional Xinisteri (70%) and Mavro (30%), sun-dried; Commandaria gold medal at Thessaloniki 2021. Tours and restaurant (11:00–19:00) with village views.
data.wineries.ktima-vassiliades.localSec: Their Commandaria won the only gold for Cyprus at Thessaloniki 2021.
data.wineries.ktima-vassiliades.name: Ktima Vassiliades
data.wineries.ktima-vassiliades.winterTi: In the heart of Omodos. Combine tour with Playia restaurant.
data.wineries.kyperounta.backstory: Production since 1998; 12 ha, gravity-fed winery, ~300,000 bottles/year.
data.wineries.kyperounta.bestTimeToVisit: Dec or Mar. Avoid peak snow Jan–Feb.
data.wineries.kyperounta.description: At 1,400 m, Kyperounta is Europe's highest winery. Established in the late 1990s, it began production in 1998. Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, and premium EPOS range benefit from slow ripening and mountain clarity. Three-level gravity-fed facility; underground cellar with 250 oak barrels. Call ahead—the road can close in snow.
data.wineries.kyperounta.localSecret: High-altitude Chardonnay and Cabernet—minerality and clarity you won't find at sea level.
data.wineries.kyperounta.name: Kyperounta Winery
data.wineries.kyperounta.openingHours: By appointment. Call for hours; road conditions vary Dec–Feb.
data.wineries.kyperounta.transport: 50 km from Limassol, 75 km from Nicosia. Pitsilia, Troodos.
data.wineries.kyperounta.winterTip: Call ahead Jan–Feb; snow can close the road. Wrap up warm. December or March are safer.
data.wineries.lambouri.description: Family winery in the heart of Krasochoria. Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Commandaria. The village of Koilani has ten wineries; Lambouri holds its own. Cosy tasting room. Book ahead. Combine with Omodos, Lania, or a full Krasochoria loop. Winter: heaters, mountain views, unhurried tastings.
data.wineries.lambouri.localSecret: The heart of Krasochoria. Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Commandaria. Book and savour.
data.wineries.lambouri.name: Lambouri Winery
data.wineries.lambouri.winterTip: Cosy tasting room; heaters in winter. Koilani has ten wineries; Lambouri is a standout.
data.wineries.linos.description: Troodos foothills. Near Platres; combine with Caledonia Falls or Artemis. Small production, mountain character. Xynisteri, reds. Call ahead. Winter: the mountains are the draw; a winery stop adds depth. Cosy tasting room.
data.wineries.linos.localSecret: Troodos foothills. Small-batch. Trail and wine in one day.
data.wineries.linos.name: Linos Winery
data.wineries.linos.winterTip: Near Platres. Combine with Caledonia or Artemis. Mountain character.
data.wineries.loel.description: Established 1943—Cyprus's first public company in wine. LOEL invested in a state-of-the-art winery at Ayios Silas in 2020, producing fine wines from indigenous varieties. They support local growers with annual grape purchases. Modern facility, heritage brand. Tastings and tours; book ahead. Easy access from Limassol. Combine with Kolossi, Kourion, or Zambartas for a coastal–vineyard day.
data.wineries.loel.localSecret: Cyprus's first public wine company. The 2020 facility is worth seeing.
data.wineries.loel.name: LOEL Winery
data.wineries.loel.winterTip: State-of-the-art facility. Heritage meets modern. Easy drive from Limassol.
data.wineries.loukas.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; do village first, then tasting.
data.wineries.loukas.description: Walk from the monastery square. Stone arches, village charm. One of the few Omodos wineries where you can drop in without a reservation. Commandaria, Xynisteri, Mavro. Do the village first; the cobbles, the kafenions; then Loukas for a tasting. Ideal for first-timers. The square is five minutes away.
data.wineries.loukas.localSecret: One of the few Omodos wineries where you can drop in. Ideal for first-timers.
data.wineries.loukas.name: Loukas Winery
data.wineries.loukas.transport: Omodos village centre; 5 min from monastery square.
data.wineries.loukas.winterTip: Walk from monastery square. No reservation needed. Stone arches, village charm.
data.wineries.makarounas.description: Boutique family winery; four generations. Only Cyprus winery sourcing exclusively from own vineyards—17–28 ha at 400–600 m. Ungrafted vines, organic viticulture. Xynisteri, Morokanella, Spourtiko, Maratheftiko, Yiannoudi, Lefkada. Decanter and international awards.
data.wineries.makarounas.localSecret: Only winery in Cyprus with 100% estate grapes. Lefkada is a standout.
data.wineries.makarounas.name: Makarounas Winery
data.wineries.makarounas.winterTip: 14 km east of Paphos. Terrace views; book ahead.
data.wineries.makrikontas.description: Vouni village, Krasochoria. Boutique production. Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Commandaria. The village is quiet; the winery welcomes visitors who book. Combine with Omodos, Lania, or Silikou. Winter: peaceful, personal. A hidden Krasochoria stop.
data.wineries.makrikontas.localSecret: A hidden stop. Boutique. Personal. The village rewards those who find it.
data.wineries.makrikontas.name: Makrikontas Winery
data.wineries.makrikontas.transport: Vouni village, Krasochoria. ~40 min from Limassol.
data.wineries.makrikontas.winterTip: Quiet Vouni. Book ahead. Hidden Krasochoria. Omodos and Lania nearby.
data.wineries.mallia.description: KEO's historic winery since 1927, at the entrance to Mallia village. Fifty hectares of estate vineyards, major production hub, and research centre for indigenous grape revival. Maratheftiko, Yiannoudi, Xynisteri, Commandaria St. John. Tours and tastings; book ahead. The scale is industrial but the story is Cypriot—KEO helped put Cypriot wine on the map. Combine with Kolossi, Kourion, or a coastal drive.
data.wineries.mallia.localSecret: Their Heritage Maratheftiko and Commandaria St. John. Indigenous variety research.
data.wineries.mallia.name: KEO Mallia Winery
data.wineries.mallia.winterTip: Major production site. Book ahead for tours. Heritage and scale.
data.wineries.meletiou.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; combine with Adonis or Aphrodite trail.
data.wineries.meletiou.description: On the Akamas wine route with sweeping sea and vineyard views. Commandaria and dry wines from the Kathikas hills. Terrace looks out over the coast; on a clear winter day the horizon stretches. Kathikas village does lunch nearby. The drive through the Akamas wine villages is half the pleasure.
data.wineries.meletiou.localSecret: Sit outside if mild. The sweep of the coast from the terrace is among the best in the Akamas villages.
data.wineries.meletiou.name: Meletiou Winery
data.wineries.meletiou.winterTip: Terrace catches afternoon sun. Kathikas village does lunch.
data.wineries.minous.description: Traditional village winery in Pachna, Commandaria heartland at 750–800 m. Generations of wine; Commandaria, Mavro, Xynisteri. Simple tasting room. Call ahead; drop-ins possible but winter hours flexible. Village tavernas nearby for lunch.
data.wineries.minous.name: Minous Winery
data.wineries.minous.winterTip: Call ahead. Pachna tavernas do lunch. Stone holds the sun in winter.
data.wineries.monagri.description: Monagri village, deep in Commandaria country. Cooperative production. Ask for the cellar tour; the story of how these villages have made wine for centuries is worth hearing. Groups welcome. Call ahead. Traditional Mavro, Xynisteri, and Commandaria. The kind of place where community and wine are inseparable.
data.wineries.monagri.localSecret: Ask for the cellar tour. Deep Commandaria country. The cooperative story is worth hearing.
data.wineries.monagri.name: Monagri Winery
data.wineries.monagri.winterTip: Monagri cooperative. Commandaria zone. Cellar tours. Groups welcome.
data.wineries.monolithos.description: Boutique winery near the Commandaria zone. Small production, quality focus. Their wines sit between tradition and modern craft. Call ahead; they welcome visitors who appreciate the small scale. Souni is off the main Krasochoria loop—fewer crowds, more conversation. Combine with Omodos, Kolossi, or a Limassol coast day.
data.wineries.monolithos.localSecret: Near Commandaria country but not in the thick of it. A quieter stop.
data.wineries.monolithos.name: Monolithos Boutique Winery
data.wineries.monolithos.winterTip: Off the main loop. Call ahead. Boutique character.
data.wineries.mystes.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; valley views from terrace.
data.wineries.mystes.description: Founded 2013. Loucas Papaloucas, winemaker (ex-Kamanterena), blends tradition and innovation; minimal intervention. At 550 m, ~33 km east of Paphos. Chardonnay, Syrah rosé, Maratheftiko; Giannoudi, Promara, Orange Xynisteri. Labels use Linear B ideograms for 'wine.' Stone and modern architecture; cheese and charcuterie platters.
data.wineries.mystes.localSecret: Linear B labels. Ask about organic practices. Promara and Orange Xynisteri surprise.
data.wineries.mystes.name: Mystes Winery
data.wineries.mystes.transport: Pano Archimandrita, 550 m. ~33 km from Paphos.
data.wineries.mystes.winterTip: 33 km east of Paphos. Book ahead. Indigenous varieties—Giannoudi, Promara, Orange Xynisteri.
data.wineries.nichteri.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; combine with Paphos hills loop.
data.wineries.nichteri.description: Small winery on the western Laona route in a restored stone building. Indigenous varieties, boutique production, intimate tastings. Stone walls hold warmth in winter; the pace slows. Western Laona has a different character—quieter, more remote. Combine with Chrysorrogiatissa or Vouni Panayia.
data.wineries.nichteri.localSecret: Western Laona villages are quieter. The detour rewards.
data.wineries.nichteri.name: Nichteri Winery
data.wineries.nichteri.winterTip: Call ahead; they appreciate notice. Stone walls hold warmth.
data.wineries.nicolaides.description: Pitsilia wine route. High-altitude vineyards; crisp whites, structured reds. Family-run. The drive up is scenic. Book ahead. Combine with Kykkos, Pedoulas, or Troodos trails. Winter: can be cooler at elevation; the tasting room warms you. Authentic mountain wine.
data.wineries.nicolaides.localSecret: Mountain terroir. Crisp, structured. The drive rewards.
data.wineries.nicolaides.name: Nicolaides Winery
data.wineries.nicolaides.winterTip: High-altitude Pitsilia. Cooler in winter. Tasting room warms you. Kykkos nearby.
data.wineries.oenou-yi.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; combine with Omodos loop.
data.wineries.oenou-yi.description: Oenou Yi (Ktima Vassiliades) established 2018. Private vineyards, some over 120 years old, on Afamis and Laona hills. ~250,000 bottles/year; indigenous Mavro, Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Lefkada, Promara, Vasilissa, Yiannoudi; Commandaria. Modern underground facility. 10:00–17:00 daily.
data.wineries.oenou-yi.localSecret: Ask about limited releases. Some vines over 120 years old.
data.wineries.oenou-yi.name: Oenou Yi Winery
data.wineries.oenou-yi.winterTip: Do monastery and village first, then Oenou Yi. Mountain views from facility.
data.wineries.olympus-winery.description: Established 1996 on the foothills of Olympus. Maratheftiko, Xinisteri, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay. Tours through barrel room and bottling line. Professional staff, positive reviews. Near Troodos; road can be snowy Jan–Feb—call ahead.
data.wineries.olympus-winery.name: Olympus Wineries
data.wineries.olympus-winery.winterTip: Combine with ski or hike. Road can be snowy Jan–Feb; call ahead.
data.wineries.papaioannou.description: Boutique winery in Vasa Koilaniou, one of the Krasochoria heartland villages. Mavro, Maratheftiko, Xynisteri, plus international varieties. Their grand stone cellar was built by local masons. Relaxed, welcoming atmosphere; staff speak English, Russian, Greek. Open daily; check hours in winter. The Petra white and red blends showcase local varieties. Groups welcome. Vasa sits between Omodos and Koilani—easy to combine with a full Krasochoria loop.
data.wineries.papaioannou.localSecret: Their Petra white and red blends. Ask about them. Vasa is quieter than Omodos.
data.wineries.papaioannou.name: Papaioannou Winery
data.wineries.papaioannou.winterTip: Vasa village. The grand cellar is worth seeing. Groups welcome. Combine with Koilani and Vlassides.
data.wineries.petrides.description: Phinikas. Off the beaten path. Boutique Xynisteri and Maratheftiko, valley views from the terrace. The drive rewards. Call ahead; they run a small operation and appreciate the notice. Intimate. Quiet. The kind of tasting where you sit and the afternoon slips away. Western Laona has a different vibe to the main wine loop.
data.wineries.petrides.localSecret: Valley from terrace. Phinikas off the beaten path. The drive rewards.
data.wineries.petrides.name: Petrides Winery
data.wineries.petrides.winterTip: Western Paphos. Phinikas. Boutique. Valley views. Book ahead.
data.wineries.pittali.description: A family passion project in the Pitsilia mountains. Fanis Pittalis returned to his ancestral village and rescued forgotten vineyards. His great-grandfather planted vines in 1910; today Pittali honours that legacy with small-scale winemaking that balances tradition and innovation. Old and new vineyards. Book ahead; they run a lean operation. The Pitsilia light in winter is sharp. Combine with Madari Ridge or Kyperounta for a full mountain day.
data.wineries.pittali.localSecret: Their great-grandfather planted vines in 1910. The story is in every bottle. Ask about the rescued old vineyards.
data.wineries.pittali.name: Pittali Winery
data.wineries.pittali.winterTip: High-altitude Pitsilia. Call ahead. Combine with Madari Ridge walk. The mountain does the work.
data.wineries.povis.description: Small family winery in the Laona hills. Low-intervention wines; Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, Mavro. The tasting room is intimate. Call ahead—they welcome visitors who appreciate the craft. Pano Panayia village; Chrysorrogiatissa Monastery nearby. Combine with the monastery, Vouni Panayia winery, or a Laona loop. Winter: cosy and unhurried.
data.wineries.povis.localSecret: Low-intervention. The family often leads the tasting. Unhurried.
data.wineries.povis.name: Povis Winery
data.wineries.povis.winterTip: Small and personal. Call ahead. Chrysorrogiatissa Monastery nearby.
data.wineries.revecca.description: Small-batch Commandaria in Agios Mamas. Traditional methods, sun-dried grapes, time in the barrel. Revecca is one of the quieter names on the Commandaria route—fewer visitors, more room to talk. Call ahead; they run a lean operation. Agios Mamas village sits in the heart of the zone. Combine with Karseras, Savvas, or Silikou Museum for a full Commandaria day.
data.wineries.revecca.localSecret: Traditional sun-dried grapes. The way it used to be done. Fewer visitors, more story.
data.wineries.revecca.name: Revecca Traditional Winery
data.wineries.revecca.winterTip: Small-batch. Call ahead. Agios Mamas is quiet Commandaria country.
data.wineries.santo.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar, 12:00–14:00 or late afternoon for golden hour.
data.wineries.santo.description: Hilltop winery above Limassol with panoramic sea and vineyard views. The restaurant serves lunch year-round; on mild winter days the terrace offers heaters and blankets. Sunset in December is around five—time a late afternoon tasting for the golden hour. Book ahead at weekends.
data.wineries.santo.localSecret: Ask for a wine-paired lunch with Cypriot meze.
data.wineries.santo.name: Santo Winery
data.wineries.santo.winterTip: Book lunch for sea views; the terrace fills at weekends. Sunset in Dec is ~17:00.
data.wineries.savvas.description: Silikou at 650 m—one of 14 villages authorised for Commandaria. Winemaking since Frankish times (~1200). Old vines, centuries of tradition. Commandaria from the heart of the zone. Off the main loop; fewer visitors, more room to breathe. Commandaria Museum nearby.
data.wineries.savvas.localSecret: Ask about the old vines. Silikou is off the main loop. Worth the detour.
data.wineries.savvas.name: Savvas Winery
data.wineries.savvas.winterTip: Combine with Commandaria Museum in Silikou. Stone cellar, centuries of tradition.
data.wineries.semeli.description: Nicosia district winery. Vineyards in the Mesaoria and foothills. Modern approach, indigenous and international varieties. Tasting room; book ahead. Combine with Lefkara, Machairas, or a Nicosia hinterland day. Winter: quiet, focused tastings. About 40 minutes from the capital.
data.wineries.semeli.localSecret: Mesaoria terroir. Modern craft. A capital escape.
data.wineries.semeli.name: Semeli Winery
data.wineries.semeli.winterTip: Nicosia's closest quality winery. Combine with Lefkara or Machairas. Book ahead.
data.wineries.silikou-museum.description: The Commandaria Museum in Silikou celebrates one of Cyprus's oldest and most famous sweet wines. Historic village, 650 metres altitude, stone presses and exhibits. The museum explains how Commandaria grapes were sun-dried and vinified using traditional methods. Also displays olive-oil equipment and household items. Silikou sits in the heart of the Commandaria zone; the Savvas winery is nearby. Contact the village before you go to confirm opening hours and whether tastings are available.
data.wineries.silikou-museum.localSecret: The traditional presses and vats tell the story of Commandaria. Savvas Winery is minutes away—do both in one afternoon.
data.wineries.silikou-museum.name: Silikou Commandaria Museum
data.wineries.silikou-museum.winterTip: Call ahead. Silikou is off the main loop; fewer visitors, more room to breathe. Combine with Savvas winery for a full Commandaria day.
data.wineries.sodap.description: Historic cooperative since 1943. One of Cyprus's largest; the story of Cypriot wine in one place. Tours of the facility, tastings, shop. Industrial scale but heritage heart. Limassol seafront. Combine with Kolossi, Kourion, or a city explore. Winter: fewer crowds, full tours available.
data.wineries.sodap.localSecret: SODAP helped build modern Cypriot wine. The cooperative story. Tours worth booking.
data.wineries.sodap.name: SODAP Winery
data.wineries.sodap.openingHours: By appointment; book ahead for tours.
data.wineries.sodap.winterTip: Historic cooperative. Industrial scale, heritage story. Easy from Limassol centre.
data.wineries.solia.description: Boutique Nicosia winery. Small production, quality focus. Xynisteri, Maratheftiko. The tasting experience is intimate. Call ahead. Combine with Agros, Machairas, or Kalopanagiotis for a mountain day. Winter: cosy, personal. Off the main wine routes—discovery territory.
data.wineries.solia.localSecret: Discovery territory. Small-batch, personal. The Nicosia hills surprise.
data.wineries.solia.name: Solia Winery
data.wineries.solia.winterTip: Off the main routes. Intimate. Combine with Agros or Machairas.
data.wineries.stavrinos.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; claim a seat by the fire.
data.wineries.stavrinos.description: Dhoros village. Mountain views. The fireplace is the draw. Book ahead and claim a seat. Their rosé is crisp even in winter; ask about it. Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, the Troodos out the window. Cosy. Stay awhile. Winter tastings here feel like the reason you came.
data.wineries.stavrinos.localSecret: Rosé is crisp even in winter. Ask. The fireplace is the draw.
data.wineries.stavrinos.name: Stavrinos Winery
data.wineries.stavrinos.winterTip: Fireplace tastings. Book ahead. Mountain views and fire—winter favourite.
data.wineries.sterna-boutique.bestTimeTo: Dec to Mar; combine with Adonis or Aphrodite trail.
data.wineries.sterna-boutique.descriptio: Family-run since 1995. ~55 ha in Kathikas. Ancient cave cellar—wine storage since Hellenistic times (2,000+ years); 15–16°C year-round. Koralli (red/white), Kelaidonis (red/white/rosé), Mayoklima Merlot. Museum with old tools. Tastings €5 with olives, bread, cheese platters. 9:30–18:00 daily.
data.wineries.sterna-boutique.localSecre: Koralli and Kelaidonis—rare indigenous varieties. Cave maintains 15–16°C.
data.wineries.sterna-boutique.name: Sterna Boutique Winery & Museum
data.wineries.sterna-boutique.winterTip: Ancient cave cellar is the draw. Kathikas village does lunch.
data.wineries.sygkrasi.description: Kathikas village, Akamas edge. On the Laona–Akamas wine route. Combine with Adonis, Aphrodite, or The Farmyard for lunch. Boutique; Xynisteri, Maratheftiko. Book ahead. Winter: the Akamas loop; trail in the morning, wine and lunch after. Coastal-meets-mountain.
data.wineries.sygkrasi.localSecret: Coastal-meets-mountain. Kathikas sits at the edge. Boutique, personal.
data.wineries.sygkrasi.name: Sygkrasi Winery
data.wineries.sygkrasi.transport: Kathikas village. On the Akamas–Laona loop.
data.wineries.sygkrasi.winterTip: Kathikas. Akamas loop. Trail in the morning, wine after. The Farmyard for lunch.
data.wineries.syndesmos.description: Cooperative on the Laona route. Community-driven, traditional methods. Ask how it works; the story is part of the tasting. Agios Georgios village is quiet. Good for a slow afternoon. Call ahead. Groups welcome. It's the kind of place that shows you how wine holds villages together.
data.wineries.syndesmos.localSecret: Ask how the cooperative works. The story is part of the tasting. Agios Georgios is quiet.
data.wineries.syndesmos.name: Syndesmos Winery
data.wineries.syndesmos.winterTip: Cooperative; community-driven. Call ahead. Groups welcome.
data.wineries.tria-elit.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; combine with Kourion or harbour lunch.
data.wineries.tria-elit.description: Modern winery near Limassol with terrace views over the Mediterranean. Experimental blends and contemporary styles. ~20 min by car from the coast—combine with harbour lunch or Kourion. Terrace catches winter sun.
data.wineries.tria-elit.name: Tria Elit Winery
data.wineries.tria-elit.winterTip: Terrace catches winter sun. Easy half-day from Limassol.
data.wineries.tsangarides.backstory: Angelos Tsangarides, 18+ years experience, revived family vineyards.
data.wineries.tsangarides.description: Founded in 2005 by Angelos Tsangarides, the estate has ~20 ha of certified organic vineyards and seven organic labels. Single Vineyard Xynisteri, Vasilissa Maratheftiko, Angels Rosé. No synthetic pesticides or chemical fertilisers. Stone-built tasting room with mountain views.
data.wineries.tsangarides.localSecret: Adopt-a-Vine club: adopt a vine, harvest, receive your case. Ask about it.
data.wineries.tsangarides.name: Tsangarides Winery
data.wineries.tsangarides.winterTip: Stone-built tasting room is cosy. Laona route—combine with Vouni Panayia.
data.wineries.tsiakkas.backstory: Founded by Costas and Marina Tsiakka. Organic since 1995, EMAS certified 2012. Four collections: Familiar, Autochton, Noble, Ambassadors. Petralona vineyard at 1,460m is among the highest in Europe.
data.wineries.tsiakkas.description: Founded in 1988, Tsiakkas sits at 1,000 m in Pelendri, Pitsilia. Thirteen hectares of certified organic vineyards produce around 200,000 bottles of Xynisteri, Maratheftiko, and indigenous varieties. The terrace has heaters in winter; guided tours run Mon–Sat at 12:00 and 14:00. Reserve ahead—the family often pours.
data.wineries.tsiakkas.localSecret: They'll point you to the best halloumi in Pelendri for a proper pairing.
data.wineries.tsiakkas.name: Tsiakkas Winery
data.wineries.tsiakkas.openingHours: Mon–Fri 10:00–16:00, Sat 11:00–17:00. Closed Sun except select dates.
data.wineries.tsiakkas.winterTip: Heated terrace in winter. Ask about the Xynisteri lees-aged.
data.wineries.vasilikon.backstory: One of Cyprus's first terroir-focused wineries; 350,000 bottles/year.
data.wineries.vasilikon.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar; restaurant at lunch.
data.wineries.vasilikon.description: Established in 1993 by the Kyriakides brothers. Sixteen hectares at 650–700 m; limestone and volcanic soils; sea breezes give a distinctive saline character. PDO Vasilikon Xynisteri (Laona Akamas since 2016), Ayios Onoufrios red (Silver 2014 International Challenge). Cellar, museum, restaurant, terrace.
data.wineries.vasilikon.localSecret: Ayios Onoufrios—their signature red. Methy (Cabernet), Aeon (Maratheftiko).
data.wineries.vasilikon.name: Vasilikon Winery
data.wineries.vasilikon.winterTip: Combine with Adonis or Aphrodite trail. Kathikas is on the Akamas loop.
data.wineries.vlassides.backstory: Third-generation winemaker; Sophocles Vlassides studied at UC Davis.
data.wineries.vlassides.description: Founded by Sophocles Vlassides (UC Davis), completed 2012. Unconventional architecture—represented Cyprus at the Mies van der Rohe Award 2015. Twenty-one hectares at 700–1,100 m. Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc; minimal oak, fruit-forward style. Rainbow tasting €7.50; 4×4 with cheese €18; Riedel experience €220.
data.wineries.vlassides.localSecret: Riedel glass tasting and Blind Tasting Challenge—unique experiences.
data.wineries.vlassides.name: Domaine Vlassides
data.wineries.vlassides.openingHours: Mon–Fri 11:00–16:00 by appointment. Closed Sun & holidays.
data.wineries.vlassides.transport: Koilani. From Ayios Amvrosios, follow Vouni–Kilani; sign 1.5 km past Vouni.
data.wineries.vlassides.winterTip: Book at least 1 day ahead. Shiraz and Cabernet are standouts.
data.wineries.vouni-panayia.backstory: Small regional winery since 1987; modern tech and museum after renovation.
data.wineries.vouni-panayia.bestTimeToVi: Dec to Feb, 2–3 hours. Combine with lunch in Panayia village.
data.wineries.vouni-panayia.description: Established in 1987, Vouni Panayia sits on a hill above Panayia village with views over Kannaviou Reservoir and the Troodos. After recent renovations it offers an educational film, traditional museum, and tasting room. Commandaria, dry whites, and robust reds from limestone-rich soils. The restaurant serves meals with valley views.
data.wineries.vouni-panayia.localSecret: The Panayia church has a revered icon; locals often combine a quick stop.
data.wineries.vouni-panayia.name: Vouni Panayia Winery
data.wineries.vouni-panayia.transport: Archiepiskopou Makariou III Ave 60, Panayia 8640. Laona route.
data.wineries.vouni-panayia.winterTip: Ask for a comparative Commandaria tasting—younger and older vintages side by side.
data.wineries.yiannis.description: Kilani village. Family estate. Their Lefkada has character; indigenous red, worth asking about. The Krasochoria hospitality is warm. Kilani is quieter than Omodos. Reserve for winter. Combine with Koilani and Vlassides for a full village day. The kind of place where someone pours and then sits down to talk.
data.wineries.yiannis.localSecret: Lefkada—indigenous red. Ask. Village atmosphere is the draw.
data.wineries.yiannis.name: Yiannis Winery
data.wineries.yiannis.winterTip: Kilani is quieter than Omodos. Reserve for winter. Combine with Koilani and Vlassides.
data.wineries.zambartas.backstory: Dr. Akis Zambartas pioneered modern Cypriot wine; Marcos Zambartas continues the family craft.
data.wineries.zambartas.bestTimeToVisit: Dec to Mar, 14:00–16:00 for a quiet tasting.
data.wineries.zambartas.description: Founded in 2006 by Dr. Akis Zambartas, the winery focuses on indigenous varieties and environmentally friendly practice. Their Shiraz–Lefkada blend is a flagship, matured 12 months in oak. Three tasting experiences: Winemaker's Selection (€20), Seasonal Selection (€15), Wine & Canapés (€25). Winter hours 10:00–17:00 weekdays, 18:00 weekends.
data.wineries.zambartas.localSecret: Ask about the PDO and Single Vineyard indigenous wines—limited production.
data.wineries.zambartas.name: Zambartas Wineries
data.wineries.zambartas.transport: Agios Amvrosios, Krasochoria. ~25 min from Limassol.
data.wineries.zambartas.winterTip: 25 min from Limassol. Winemaker's Selection includes exclusive Commandaria barrel sample.
data.wineries.zambeli.description: Family winery on the Limassol wine route. Traditional and modern. Commandaria, dry whites, reds. Cosy tasting. Book ahead. Combine with Kolossi, Kourion, or Omodos. Winter: heaters, unhurried. The Limassol corridor has many options; Zambeli is a quiet favourite.
data.wineries.zambeli.localSecret: Traditional and modern. Commandaria and dry wines. Unhurried.
data.wineries.zambeli.name: Zambeli Winery
data.wineries.zambeli.winterTip: Quiet favourite on the Limassol corridor. Heaters in winter. Kolossi and Kourion nearby.
data.wineRoutes.akamas.description: Kathikas and the Akamas peninsula. Combine with Adonis Trail, Baths of Aphrodite. Rustic charm.
data.wineRoutes.akamas.title: Akamas
data.wineRoutes.commandaria.description: Cyprus's oldest wine. Sweet, sun-dried. Omodos, Pera Pedi, Silikou, Kilani. UNESCO heritage.
data.wineRoutes.commandaria.title: Commandaria
data.wineRoutes.krasochoria.description: The wine villages of Limassol. Omodos, Koilani, Pera Pedi, Pelendri. Mountain views, indigenous varieties, Commandaria.
data.wineRoutes.krasochoria.title: Krasochoria
data.wineRoutes.laona.description: Paphos hill villages. Panayia, Lemona, Stroumbi. Cozy tastings, old vines, winter fireside.
data.wineRoutes.laona.title: Laona
data.winterTips.book-ahead.body: Many wineries run small operations. In winter they appreciate a call or online booking. You'll often get the owner or winemaker pouring. Worth the extra step.
data.winterTips.book-ahead.title: Book winery tastings ahead
data.winterTips.check-conditions.body: Troodos weather changes fast. Snow on Olympus, mud after rain, ice on shaded sections. The ski resort posts conditions. So do local cafés. Ask. Don't assume.
data.winterTips.check-conditions.title: Check before you go
data.winterTips.daylight.body: Sunrise around 6:45am, sunset around 5pm in December and January. Plan outdoor activities for the morning. By 4pm the light is already golden. Use it.
data.winterTips.daylight.title: Daylight is short
data.winterTips.drive-left.body: British legacy. Rent a car if you want to reach villages and trails. The roads are good. Mountain bends can be tight. Take your time. The views are worth it.
data.winterTips.drive-left.title: Drive on the left
data.winterTips.emergency.body: 112 for EU emergency. 1460 for tourist information. 199 for ambulance. Save them. Hope you never need them.
data.winterTips.emergency.title: Emergency numbers
data.winterTips.euro.body: Cyprus uses the euro. Cards work almost everywhere. Small village shops and kafenions sometimes prefer cash. Keep €20 or so for coffee, lace, and zivania.
data.winterTips.euro.title: Euro, cards, and cash
data.winterTips.kafenion-stop.body: Village kafenions are where locals meet. Order a Greek coffee, sit, watch. No rush. In winter the stove is lit and the pace is slow. The person at the next table often knows the best winery, trail, or taverna. The best advice isn't in a guidebook.
data.winterTips.kafenion-stop.title: Stop for a coffee
data.winterTips.layers.body: The coast might be 18°C while Troodos is 5°C. Bring a windproof jacket, a warm mid-layer, and a hat. Mountain cafés have fireplaces. Coastal tavernas have heaters. Dress for both.
data.winterTips.layers.title: Layer up
data.winterTips.microspikes.body: Olympus Summit and higher Troodos trails can have snow and ice from January to March. Microspikes cost €20 and fit over your boots. If the forecast is near freezing, bring them.
data.winterTips.microspikes.title: Microspikes for Olympus
data.winterTips.start-early.body: Winter daylight ends around 5pm. Give yourself time to finish in the light. The morning air is crisp. The trails are empty. You'll thank yourself when you're back at the car by 3.
data.winterTips.start-early.title: Start by 9am
data.winterTips.tell-someone.body: Phone signal is patchy in the mountains. Tell your hotel or a friend which trail you're on and when you expect back. Emergency: 112. The mountain doesn't care about your deadline.
data.winterTips.tell-someone.title: Tell someone your route
data.winterTips.weekday-quiet.body: Omodos, Lefkara, and the main sites fill up on weekends. Tuesday or Wednesday? You'll have the cobbles to yourself. Villages feel different when the tour buses have gone. Plan big days for midweek.
data.winterTips.weekday-quiet.title: Weekdays are quieter
data.winterTips.winter-light.body: Winter sun is lower. Golden hour starts around 3:30pm in December. Ancient sites, villages, the coast: everything looks different. Bring a camera. Or just watch. The light alone is worth the trip. Plan ruins and villages for the afternoon and you'll see why.
data.winterTips.winter-light.title: The light is different
